solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Star, a bit dim, is embarrassed and diminutive

parts.note: someone embarrassed goes red in the face
a dwarf is something very small, a diminutive one

explanation.surface: A faint star is described as blushing and tiny.
explanation.definitionFit: A red dwarf is a small, cool star of low luminosity, hence a bit dim.

clue.text: No rice pudding for Caruso, for instance

indicators.note: pudding suggests a mixed-up mash, so these six letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: The great tenor is declared to have refused rice pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pudding' looks like dessert, but it signals the anagram of NO RICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Enrico Caruso was the famous Italian operatic tenor; the forename is defined by example.

clue.text: Old-fashioned but popular with the boys

definitions.meaning: out of date, no longer in style
went out on romantic outings with young men, as a sought-after girl did

explanation.surface: A girl is described as out of style yet much sought after by young men.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: no longer current, and having gone out with suitors on romantic outings.

clue.text: Escort agency is brought to account

indicators.note: the agency is brought up to follow the account, so it comes after

parts.note: a company is a business or agency

explanation.surface: An escort agency faces having its books examined.
explanation.definitionFit: To escort someone is to go along with them as company, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Rugby player is crafty one of a pair

parts.note: fly is informal British for sharp or cunning
each of two equal parts is a half

explanation.surface: A rugby player is described as cunning and one of two.
explanation.walkthrough: FLY in the sense 'knowing, sly' is British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: The fly-half is the rugby union back who wears number 10 and directs play.

clue.text: Impressive time of the year

definitions.meaning: majestic, inspiring awe and respect
the eighth month of the calendar

explanation.surface: A season is praised as grand.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective the word means grand and venerable; capitalised it is a summer month.

clue.text: A lot to collect

parts.note: a mass is a great quantity, a lot

explanation.surface: Lots of things are there to be gathered.
explanation.definitionFit: To gather together a large quantity of things is a synonym for collecting them.

clue.text: Culture for breeding

definitions.meaning: refinement and polish of manners
good family background, being of polite birth

explanation.surface: Refinement is treated as a matter of upbringing.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means refined manners and also the social standing of well-born people.

clue.text: Tolerates corporations

definitions.meaning: puts up with, can bear
jocular old word for large paunches, big bellies

explanation.surface: A company is said to put up with big businesses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corporations' looks like businesses, but it is the old joke sense of a paunch.
explanation.definitionFit: One can stomach an insult, and a corporation is a humorous term for a pot belly.

clue.text: He reviews one with opposing views

definitions.meaning: a reviewer of books, plays or films
someone who finds fault and argues against

explanation.surface: A reviewer is painted as someone who disagrees.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a professional reviewer and anyone who censures or objects.

clue.text: Really fancy outing on a ferry

indicators.note: an outing takes the letters out of their order, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Someone very much wants a boat trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outing' looks like a trip, but it signals the anagram of ON A FERRY.
explanation.definitionFit: To long for something strongly is to fancy it very much, an idiomatic match.

clue.text: A chartered accountant meant to retire for the scholastic life

indicators.note: retiring means going backwards, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: aimed is a synonym for meant or intended

explanation.surface: An accountant intended to leave work and take up study.
explanation.definitionFit: The world of universities and scholarship is the scholastic life.

clue.text: Rise in prices, perhaps, left east of Paris ruined

indicators.note: in an across answer east means to the right, so it follows
something ruined is wrecked, so the city's letters are broken up

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Prices rising leave the French capital in ruins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rise in prices' looks like the wordplay, but it is the definition; the French capital is only fodder, and 'east of' works because this is an across light.
explanation.definitionFit: An inflationary spiral is an escalating rise, so a price rise is an example.

clue.text: Few vehicles about, but this will control them

indicators.note: the two words are turned about, swapping their order

parts.note: light traffic means few vehicles on the road

explanation.surface: A traffic signal controls roads that are quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' swaps LIGHT TRAFFIC round, moving LIGHT to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A road signal with red, amber and green lamps regulates vehicles, so it controls them.

clue.text: Addressing some criticism

definitions.meaning: speaking to someone
a scolding or reprimand

explanation.surface: A speech turns out to be a reprimand.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally speaking to someone, and as a noun a telling-off or rebuke.

clue.text: List and a record used in acute novel

indicators.note: the two pieces are placed inside the rearranged letters
novel means new, so the letters are made into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
a log is a written record, as on a ship

explanation.surface: A list and a record feature in a sharp new book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'acute' looks like an adjective describing the novel, but it is the anagram fodder, and 'novel' is the signal rather than a book.
explanation.definitionFit: A catalogue is a systematic list of items, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Sit a certain way for the ideal journey?

parts.note: best means perfect, ideal
a ride is a trip or journey

explanation.surface: The best ride needs a particular way of sitting.
explanation.definitionFit: To straddle something with legs on either side is a particular way of sitting.

clue.text: Seems return for my passage will be by end of day — pity!

parts.note: it feels cold means it seems cold

indicators.note: returning brings the word back the other way round

parts.note: taken as written
a path is a way or passage

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A traveller laments the cost of a return trip at dusk.
explanation.definitionFit: To pity someone is to have compassion for them, a phrasal synonym for the verb.

clue.text: Flawlessly finished, though tense

definitions.meaning: complete and without fault
the verb tense for completed action

explanation.surface: Something is called flawless though nervy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tense' looks like nervous, but it is the grammatical tense, as in 'I have eaten'.
explanation.definitionFit: Faultless and complete, and also the name of the grammatical tense for completed action.

clue.text: Path that students may take

definitions.meaning: a route or direction followed
a programme of study

explanation.surface: A path that students follow.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a route and also a series of lessons a student enrols in.

clue.text: Horses one's used in a racket

definitions.meaning: a group of racehorses kept by one stable
the cord strung across a tennis racket

explanation.surface: A horse is used in some kind of fraud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'racket' suggests a swindle, but it is a tennis racket's gut.
explanation.definitionFit: A stable's horses are a string, and strings of gut are stretched across a racket.

clue.text: Elegance of a short prayer

definitions.meaning: poise and refinement of movement
the thanks said before a meal

explanation.surface: Elegance is attributed to a brief prayer.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means elegance of movement and the brief thanks said at table.

clue.text: Pound note put back in share account

indicators.note: the reversed pair goes inside the share

parts.note: a ration is a fixed share or allowance

indicators.note: put back means the two letters are turned round

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for pound, from libra
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: A banknote is returned to a joint account.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put back' turns LE into EL, which 'in' places after the R of RATION.
explanation.definitionFit: A relation is a narrative or telling of events, an account of them.

clue.text: Conviction that can be reversed?

indicators.note: a word that can be read backwards to the same letters

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A belief that might be overturned.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer reads the same in both directions.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenet is a firmly held belief or principle, a conviction.

clue.text: Cadger is going off in shame

indicators.note: going off suggests something spoiling or exploding, so the letters are scattered

explanation.surface: A scrounger leaves in disgrace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going off' looks like leaving, but it signals the anagram of CADGER IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Disgrace and shame are synonyms, both meaning loss of respect.

clue.text: Support attempt to back horse to come first

indicators.note: the reversed horse is placed before the attempt

parts.note: a nag is an old horse
a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: A punter decides to bet on a horse to win.
explanation.definitionFit: A gantry is a supporting frame, such as one carrying signals or a crane.

clue.text: Change into suit

definitions.meaning: turn into, grow to be
look good on, flatter

explanation.surface: Someone is told to change into a suit.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means turning into something and also flattering someone, as a colour might.

clue.text: Nurse that is meeting son's agreements

parts.note: to nurse a patient is to treat them
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A nurse meets her son's needs.
explanation.definitionFit: Treaties are formal agreements between states, a straight synonym.
